name: Preferans
description: Preferans (derived from the French 'PrÃ©fÃ©rence') is the quintessential card game of the Russian intelligentsia and one of the most intellectually demanding games in existence. Played by 3 or 4 players with a 32-card deck, it is a bidding-based trick-taking game where players compete for contracts, including the dreaded 'Misere' (taking zero tricks). history.origins: Developed in Russia in the mid-19th century from French games like 'L'Hombre' and 'Boston'. It became the preferred game of the Russian military, students, and nobility.
timeline: 1840s: First appearance in St. Petersburg gambling halls.
1890s: Rules for 'Misere' and 'Whistling' are perfected across the Russian Empire.
1910s: Tolstoy and Dostoyevsky mention Preferans in their works as a mark of a gentleman's skill.
Present: Remains a cultural institution in Russia, Ukraine, and the former Soviet states.
history.cultural: Commonly described as more a 'Social Philosophy' than a game, emphasizing honor and tactical discipline.
history.evolution: Unlike Bridge, which moved toward partnerships, Preferans remained a 'Free-for-All', where alliances shift with every 'Whistle' (the decision to defend a contract).

setup.players: Typically 3 active players. If 4, the dealer sits out and gets 'Buy-in' points.
setup.dealing: 2 cards each, 2 to the 'Talon' (the Widow), continuing until everyone has 10 cards.

rules.objective: Complete a predetermined amount of 'Bullet' points while keeping your 'Mountain' (penalty points) low.
rules.gameplay: Three or four players (dealer sits out if four). Deal: 2 cards each, 2 to talon, then 2-2-2-2 each (10 cards per player). Bidding: eldest hand starts; players bid number of tricks (6–10) and trump (spades, clubs, diamonds, hearts, no trump) or misère. Highest bidder becomes declarer, takes talon, discards two cards, declares contract. Defenders choose to whist or pass; if both pass, declarer wins without play. Play: eldest hand leads; must follow suit, else must trump if possible. Trick winner leads next. Declarer must make contracted tricks; defenders who whist must make their quota.
keyRules: Deal 10 cards each, 2 to talon; eldest hand leads bidding.
Bid tricks (6–10) and trump (spades, clubs, diamonds, hearts, no trump) or misère; highest bidder is declarer.
Declarer takes talon, discards two, declares contract; defenders choose to whist or pass.
Follow suit; when void, must trump if possible. Trick winner leads next.
Score by pool (bullet), whists, and mountain (dump penalties).

strategy.basic: Calculate your 'Safe' tricks. In Preferans, bidding is about certainty, not hope. If you have the Ace and King of a suit, that is two safe tricks. If you have 5 trumps including the Ace, you can safely bid 6. Be extremely careful with 'Misere'â€”it is high-risk, high-reward, and the defenders will play 'Crucial Card' logic to force you to take a trick.
strategy.intermediate: Whistling Discipline: Only 'Whistle' if you have 'Stop cards' (Aces or Kings). If you Whistle and fail (Get set), you lose massive points on the 'Mountain'. However, Whistling is the only way to earn 'Whist points'â€”the most valuable currency in the final score calculation. It is the art of knowing when to punish the declarer and when to let them win.
strategy.advanced: The 'Talon' Discard: The 2 cards you discard after picking up the Widow can win or lose you the game. Protect your weak suits by discarding the low cards of those suits. If you have a 'Void', you have a massive advantage in trumping the declarer's high cards. The best Preferans players treat every hand as a puzzle of 'Optimal Shedding' before the first trick is even played.
tips: In Misere, always try to keep cards that are part of a 'Gap' (e.g., 7-9-J), as this forces the opponent to play the middle cards.
Watch the 'Bullet' progress. If an opponent is about to close their Bullet, whistle more aggressively to push them into the 'Mountain'.

variations.name: Sochi scoring
variations.description: Pool, whist and dump points; declarer and defenders score or pay per contract and tricks.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Sochi scoring differs by table rules; engine constants not yet mapped.

variations.name: Rostov (Moscow) scoring
variations.description: Dump penalties for whisters halved; dump points replaced by 5 whist points per point to each opponent.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Rostov dump/whist substitution; engine constants not yet mapped.

variations.name: Misère and all-pass
variations.description: Misère: bid to take zero tricks; ranks between 8 NT and 9 spades; played at no trumps with defenders' cards face up. All-pass (raspasovka): when no one bids, each player tries to take as few tricks as possible; no trumps.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Misère and all-pass are alternate modes; overrides to be added when implemented.

scoring.winCondition: First to close the Bullet (pool) while keeping Mountain (dump penalties) low; or play to agreed match length.
